findings.body:
`deliver` now POSTs `event` to whatever `url` the caller supplies. A customer- or attacker-controlled value such as `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`, `http://127.0.0.1:6379/`, or `file:///etc/passwd` is fetched from this process; `urlopen` also follows redirects, so a public HTTPS URL can still land on an internal target.

Keep customer endpoints, but restrict the scheme to `https`, resolve the host and reject loopback/link-local/private/metadata addresses, and disable or re-validate redirects before the request is sent.

summary:
Customer webhook delivery now POSTs to an arbitrary caller-supplied URL. That is a server-side request forgery on the process that runs `deliver`.

The previous `ALLOWED_HOSTS` check was the only control that kept `url` on `hooks.internal.example`. After this hunk, `urllib.request.urlopen` follows whatever scheme, host, and port the caller provides, including loopback, link-local/metadata (`169.254.169.254`), private RFC1918 addresses, and non-HTTP schemes such as `file://`. `urlopen` also follows redirects by default, so a public HTTPS endpoint can still bounce the request onto an internal target.

Supporting customer endpoints is a reasonable product goal; it still needs an allow/deny policy that runs after DNS resolution (block loopback, link-local, private, and metadata ranges), an `https`-only scheme, and redirect re-validation. I would not ship this as-is.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch removes the ALLOWED_HOSTS check that previously rejected non-allowlisted hosts; deliver now POSTs via urllib.request.urlopen to any caller-supplied URL with no scheme, host, or redirect validation, which is a real SSRF regression.
